result.title: Not Every Cue Is Evidence: Cue Supportability for Forensic Distillation in Face Forgery Detection
result.summary: Explainable face forgery detection requires not only correct judgments but also forensic evidence supported by the input image. However, training cues are typically derived from the forgery generation pipeline. Since images available to the model are of limited quality and resolution, it is difficult to observe the fine-grained traces these cues refer to. Training methods that further supply such cues as privileged supervision exacerbate the problem, as the student is taught to articulate evidence it cannot perceive. The student consequently resorts to templated or over-generalized expressions, giving rise to the correct-answer, wrong-evidence (CAWE) failure. We propose a dual supportability audit that filters privileged cues before distillation. Each candidate cue must be predictable from the remaining privileged context and causally tied to high-attribution visual regions in the current image. Only cues satisfying both conditions receive substantial distillation weight, preventing unsupported details from leaking into the student. Experiments across eight benchmarks show that our method maintains or improves detection accuracy while significantly raising explanation faithfulness compared to existing paradigms.

AI.brief_summary: 针对人脸伪造检测中「答案正确但证据错误」的失败，提出双重可支持性审计：蒸馏前要求候选线索既能由剩余特权上下文预测、又与当前图像的高归因视觉区域因果绑定，仅满足两者才给予显著蒸馏权重。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「线索必须与图像高归因区域绑定、否则不应作为监督信号」的思路，可能与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、特权监督下的贡献分配问题相通，可供核查；但任务为单图检测，与 latent 状态生成和推理期使用距离较远。
